events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 115 AM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable. It will
take several hours for all the water from these storms to work
through local drainage systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1013 PM MST, Streamflow gauge reports indicate elevated flows
along Indian Bend Wash. Flooding is already occurring in the
warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have fallen over the
last 6 hours.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Paradise Valley and Downtown Scottsdale.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Temperatures of 36 degrees or lower will result in frost
formation.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest and west central Oregon and southwest
Washington.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a 20-30% chance that temperatures
will fall below 32 degrees, especially for locations that do not
develop fog. Frost and freeze headlines are only issued through the
growing season of April 1 through October 31. Therefore, frost or
freeze headlines will not be issued beginning November 1, even
though similar low temperatures are possible. Frost and freeze
headlines will no longer be issued this growing season for the
Upper Hood River Valley, southern Willamette Valley, south
Washington Cascade Foothills, and north Oregon Coast Range as these
locations have already experienced a hard freeze earlier in
October.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.

events.region: Aguila Valley; Northwest Valley; Tonopah Desert; Gila Bend; Buckeye/Avondale; Cave Creek/New River; Deer Valley; Central Phoenix; North Phoenix/Glendale; New River Mesa; Scottsdale/Paradise Valley; Rio Verde/Salt River; East Valley; Fountain Hills/East Mesa; South Mountain/Ahwatukee; Southeast Valley/Queen Creek; Northwest Pinal County; West Pinal County; Apache Junction/Gold Canyon; Sonoran Desert Natl Monument
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Arizona, including the following
areas, Phoenix Metro, rural areas of Maricopa County, and Northwest
Pinal County.

* WHEN...From Saturday evening through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A second, followup weather system will bring even better
atmospheric moisture over the region Saturday night through
Sunday and lead to a  prolonged period of light to moderate
rainfall across the Watch area, with embedded convection
producing pockets of heavier rain. Additional rainfall amounts on
the order of 1-2" will fall over several hours or longer on top
of already moist soil, leading to additional runoff.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: Kaibab Plateau; Marble and Glen Canyons; Grand Canyon Country; Coconino Plateau; Northeast Plateaus and Mesas Hwy 264 Northward; Chinle Valley; Chuska Mountains and Defiance Plateau; Little Colorado River Valley in Coconino County; Little Colorado River Valley in Navajo County; Little Colorado River Valley in Apache County; Western Mogollon Rim; Eastern Mogollon Rim; White Mountains; Black Mesa Area; Northeast Plateaus and Mesas South of Hwy 264
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central and northeast Arizona, including
the following areas, in north central Arizona, Black Mesa Area,
Coconino Plateau, Eastern Mogollon Rim, Grand Canyon Country,
Kaibab Plateau, Little Colorado River Valley in Coconino County,
Marble and Glen Canyons, Northeast Plateaus and Mesas Hwy 264
Northward, Northeast Plateaus and Mesas South of Hwy 264 and
Western Mogollon Rim. In northeast Arizona, Chinle Valley, Chuska
Mountains and Defiance Plateau, Little Colorado River Valley in
Apache County, Little Colorado River Valley in Navajo County and
White Mountains.

* WHEN...From Saturday evening through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A second round of rain and isolated thunderstorms is expected
Saturday night through the early morning hours of Monday. An
additional 1 to 3 inches of rain will be possible, on top of
already saturated ground, increasing the threat of flooding.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Waters from Cameron LA to High Island TX from 20 to 60 NM; Waters from Intracoastal City to Cameron LA from 20 to 60 NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWLCH

The National Weather Service in Lake Charles has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Cameron LA to High Island TX from 20 to 60 NM...
Waters from Intracoastal City to Cameron LA from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 100 AM CDT.

* At 1152 PM CDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from near West
Cameron 342 to 7 nm northwest of West Cameron 368 to West Cameron
269, moving north at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
West Cameron Wc303, West Cameron 269, West Cameron 368, West
Cameron 342, West Cameron 196, West Cameron 294, West Cameron 215,
and West Cameron 205.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 9 to 14
inches possible. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...The Klondike Highway including White Pass

* WHEN...From 10 AM AKDT Saturday to 9 AM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. Conditions
will likely become slick and hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels will start out around 600' early
Saturday morning but are expected to rise to around 1,500' by mid
day Saturday. This will limit snow accumulations for places below
milepost 10 on the Klondike Highway.
